facts.text: The opening narration is by Vic Perrin, who also secretly voices the head gargoyle. He's uncredited for the creature voice.
The whole movie was shot in just 18 days with a single camera. The first director reportedly quit because he thought that schedule was impossible.
This was Stan Winston's first professional job. He and his wife sculpted the background gargoyle masks at their dining room table in two weeks, she rolling the clay scale balls.
Watch the back seat of the station wagon: the knee of the sound man is visible behind Cornel Wilde's head.
Grayson Hall decided her character should hold a drink in every scene she appears in.
Winston threatened to quit unless the gargoyle makers got screen credit. They did, and only credited artists were Emmy-eligible. The film won the 1973 Emmy for makeup.
The gargoyle suits were neoprene wetsuits covered in fishnet and bits of rubber. Temperatures on set often topped 100F.
The hotel in the film was a real abandoned hotel near Carlsbad, New Mexico. It was actually burned down for the movie.
As the shed collapses on Uncle Willie, look at the lower right: a crew member gets knocked to the floor and scrambles out of frame.
Continuity check: the wagon's window is down as the Boleys flee, then a gargoyle smashes the driver's side glass.
Uncle Willie says the Native American name for the gargoyle is 'nakatekachinko', and the dance that summons them is 'nonataya'.
Bernie Casey's voice was replaced by Vic Perrin's in post-production because his natural voice didn't suit the head gargoyle.
Bernie Casey played for the 49ers and Rams, and was also a painter and poet. Winston owned several of his paintings.
The gargoyles' running and moving shots were slowed down to give them an unnatural, jerky quality.
Jennifer Salt is the daughter of Midnight Cowboy screenwriter Waldo Salt. She appeared in that film too, as Crazy Annie.
Around the 39-minute mark, the cameraman's shadow can be seen on a tree.
Grayson Hall was Oscar-nominated for The Night of the Iguana. She was also Dr. Julia Hoffman on Dark Shadows, a role planned to last just a few weeks.
Scott Glenn, here a biker, later starred in The Right Stuff and The Silence of the Lambs. He worked as a newspaper reporter before acting.
Cornel Wilde was picked for the 1936 US Olympic fencing team but turned it down to pursue acting. This is his only TV movie lead.
One of the stuntmen playing a biker also plays one of the gargoyles.
The credits name Ellis Burman and Stan Winston as creators of the gargoyle make-up. Winston later did Terminator, Aliens, Predator and Jurassic Park.
On the DVD cover Winston's name is most prominent. He admitted feeling embarrassed, since Sonny Burman and Del Armstrong deserved the credit more.
William Stevens, who plays the police chief, also played Officer Jerry Walters on the TV series Adam-12.
The film was written by Stephen and Elinor Karpf and aired on CBS on November 21, 1972, opposite ABC and NBC programming.
Gargoyles is referenced in Jeepers Creepers (2001), and director Bill Norton later made Convoy (1978) and a Buffy the Vampire Slayer episode.
A reviewer noted the creature design has a Sid and Marty Krofft flavor, especially in the cave birthing scenes.
The DVD version is a 74-minute European theatrical cut, slightly longer than the original US TV broadcast.
